headline: High: RD-Agent’s broad network/API access can leak or act on Great Expectations outputs, while shared-file and prompt-injection risks are limited by the profiles.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Great Expectations can read and write files for data sources and validation results, while RD-Agent can run browsers and consume files/logs. There is no documented shared channel or direct parser bridge, so prompt injection is possible mainly through manual or file-based handoff, not by default.
conditions: IF Great Expectations outputs are copied into RD-Agent prompts or browser-visible pages, injection becomes plausible.
IF both agents are pointed at the same untrusted documentation or log files, malicious instructions can traverse the handoff.
mitigations: Keep Great Expectations outputs in structured formats only.
Strip instructions from any text handed to RD-Agent.
Use separate folders for each agent's artifacts.
Review copied snippets before pasting into RD-Agent.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Great Expectations touches validation results and documentation with no network egress, but RD-Agent has broad egress and uses OpenAI/Azure/DeepSeek/Kaggle APIs plus secrets. If Great Expectations data is handed to RD-Agent, sensitive validation content can leave the local boundary through RD-Agent’s default external calls.
conditions: IF Great Expectations validation results or source data are passed into RD-Agent prompts or files, those contents can be transmitted to third-party APIs.
IF RD-Agent is configured with its listed API keys, outbound leakage risk increases for any shared sensitive data.
mitigations: Do not pass sensitive validation outputs into RD-Agent.
Disable RD-Agent API calls for sensitive runs.
Use redacted sample data only.
Rotate or scope API keys before testing.
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists and content filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Great Expectations writes data sources and validation results, while RD-Agent writes logs and supports multiple instances. The profiles do not show a shared writable directory, git state, or overlapping mutable resource, so conflict is possible only if an operator co-locates their outputs.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF an orchestrator launches multiple RD-Agent instances against shared outputs, race conditions can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Run one writer per directory.
Use timestamped filenames.
Check for existing files before overwrite.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Great Expectations produces validation results that RD-Agent could ingest as research context or logs. RD-Agent’s browser/API-enabled workflow can then act on those outputs without a documented verification gate, so a bad validation artifact can cascade into downstream actions or generated conclusions.
conditions: IF RD-Agent uses Great Expectations validation results as authoritative input, errors can propagate into generated research or API-driven actions.
IF no human review is inserted between validation output and RD-Agent consumption, cascading error risk increases.
mitigations: Require human review of validation outputs.
Feed RD-Agent only summarized, checked results.
Cross-check critical assertions against source data.
Log provenance for every imported result.
requires-engineering: add a verification stage before RD-Agent actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Great Expectations handles validation results and documentation locally, while RD-Agent processes financial reports, papers, competition datasets, logs, and sends data to external APIs. That creates a compliance mismatch risk if regulated or confidential data from Great Expectations is forwarded into RD-Agent’s third-party services; the profiles do not show matching residency or retention controls.
conditions: IF regulated data from Great Expectations is forwarded to RD-Agent APIs, residency or retention obligations may be violated.
IF the operator relies on RD-Agent logs for sensitive datasets, retention mismatch risk increases.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of RD-Agent.
Use de-identified datasets only.
Review API retention settings.
Separate logs by sensitivity class.
requires-engineering: document and enforce data-processing agreements.
